en: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.
zh: 米開朗基羅的大衛故事絕非一個少年王者殺死生命的故事。
ja: ミケランジェロのダビデの物語は、少年王が命を奪った話ではありません。
local: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.
native: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.

en: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,
zh: 在他的一首詩中，米開朗基羅寫道，
ja: 彼の詩の一つで、ミケランジェロはこう書いています、
local: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,
native: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,

en: 'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'
zh: 「Somedi ese de Broutdo，我知道我很醜。」
ja: 「Somedi ese de Broutdo、私は醜いと知っている。」
local: 'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'
native: 'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'

en: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.
zh: 他的鼻子斷了，看起來像是被壓扁在臉上，他說這讓他看起來像個乞丐。
ja: 彼の鼻は折れて顔に押しつぶされたように見え、彼はそれが乞食のように見せていると言いました。
local: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.
native: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.

en: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.
zh: 他被自己的外貌折磨，與自己的身體疏離。
ja: 彼は自分の容姿に苦しみ、自分の体から孤立していました。
local: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.
native: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.

en: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.
zh: 儘管如此，或許正因如此，他一生都在追求崇高的完美。
ja: それにもかかわらず、あるいはそのために、彼は崇高な完璧さを追求して生涯を費やしました。
local: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.
native: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.

en: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.
zh: 他對自己的外貌無能為力，但他會確保他的《大衛》成為評判男性美的標準。
ja: 彼は自分の容姿を変えることはほとんどできませんでしたが、自分のダビデ像が男性美の基準になるようにしました。
local: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.
native: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.

en: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.
zh: 米開朗基羅相信自己是上帝的工具。
ja: ミケランジェロは自分が神の道具であると信じていました。
local: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.
native: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.

en: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.
zh: 他不是從大理石創作雕塑，而是釋放被囚禁在其中的形象。
ja: 彼は大理石から彫刻を作っているのではなく、その中に閉じ込められた形を解放しているだけでした。
local: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.
native: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.

en: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.
zh: 米開朗基羅未完成的作品讓我們深入了解他的技法。
ja: ミケランジェロの未完成の作品は、彼の技術について多くの洞察を与えてくれます。
local: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.
native: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.

en: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.
zh: 大多數雕塑家會先製作泥土模型，然後在大理石上標記要敲擊的地方。
ja: ほとんどの彫刻家は粘土のモデルを作り、その後大理石の塊に刻む場所を印をつけます。
local: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.
native: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.

en: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.
zh: 但米開朗基羅大多數時間是徒手雕刻，從正面開始往後雕刻。
ja: しかしミケランジェロは主にフリーハンドで作業し、前から後ろへと進めました。
local: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.
native: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.

en: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.
zh: 雕刻大理石需要運動員的力量和外科醫生的靈巧。
ja: 大理石を彫るには、アスリートの力と外科医の器用さが必要です。
local: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.
native: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.

en: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.
zh: 任何失誤都可能毀掉多年的努力。
ja: どんなミスも何年もの努力を台無しにする可能性があります。
local: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.
native: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.

en: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,
zh: 米開朗基羅會從所謂的粗雕開始，
ja: ミケランジェロは「ラフアウト」と呼ばれる作業から始めました、
local: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,
native: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,

en: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.
zh: 用尖鑿和大錘去除大部分重量，將雕塑塑造成大致形狀。
ja: ポイントチゼルと大きな木槌を使って大部分の石を取り除き、彫刻の大まかな形にします。
local: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.
native: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.

en: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.
zh: 然後他會用齒鑿和較小的錘子進行更細緻的造型工作。
ja: 次に、歯のついたチゼルと小さなハンマーを使って、形の詳細なモデリングを行います。
local: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.
native: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.

en: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.
zh: 隨著需要更多細節，他會使用越來越細的齒鑿。
ja: より細かいディテールが必要になると、より細かい歯のついたチゼルを使いました。
local: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.
native: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.

en: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.
zh: 他會用鑽子鑽入更深的裂縫。
ja: 彼はより深い隙間に入るためにドリルを使いました。
local: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.
native: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.

en: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.
zh: 然後他會用各種小工具進行精細修飾，最後用銼刀等工具完成表面處理。
ja: その後、様々な小さな道具を使って仕上げを行い、ラスプのようなやすりで表面を整えました。
local: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.
native: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.

en: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.
zh: 最後，他會用磨蝕性的浮石和皮革拋光雕像，直到表面光滑有光澤。
ja: 最後に、研磨性のある軽石と革を使って彫像を磨き、滑らかで光沢のある仕上がりにしました。
local: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.
native: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.

en: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.
zh: 如果我們看他未完成的作品，可以清楚看到雕塑從石頭中浮現。
ja: ここにある彼の未完成の作品を見ると、彫刻が石から浮かび上がってくるのがはっきりとわかります。
local: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.
native: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.

en: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.
zh: 我們看到的這些痕跡是米開朗基羅親手留下的。
ja: ここに見える跡はミケランジェロ自身の手によるものです。
local: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.
native: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.

en: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.
zh: 外部部分顯示米開朗基羅用大鑿和錘子開始切割石頭的地方。
ja: 外側の部分は、ミケランジェロが大きなピックと木槌で石を切り始めた場所を示しています。
local: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.
native: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.

en: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.
zh: 在這個區域，我們可以清楚看到他使用了齒鑿。
ja: そしてこの部分では、彼が歯のついたチゼルを使ったのがはっきり見えます。
local: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.
native: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.

en: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.
zh: 在胸部這裡，我們看到更多細節和更細微的痕跡，顯示他使用了更精細的工具。
ja: 胸の部分では、さらに細かいディテールと、より細かい道具を使った跡が見られます。
local: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.
native: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.

en: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.
zh: 米開朗基羅26歲時被委託雕刻聖經英雄大衛的巨大雕像。
ja: ミケランジェロは26歳の時に、聖書の英雄ダビデの巨大な像を彫るよう依頼されました。
local: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.
native: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.

en: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.
zh: 將被放置在大教堂屋頂上，距街道80米高。
ja: 大聖堂の屋根に設置される予定で、地上80メートルの高さです。
local: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.
native: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.

en: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.
zh: 就在兩年前，他在羅馬雕刻了令人心痛的美麗彼得，他已被視為大師。
ja: わずか2年前に彼はローマで痛ましいほど美しいピエタを彫刻し、すでに名匠と見なされていました。
local: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.
native: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.

en: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.
zh: 他被要求使用大教堂已有的舊大理石塊，已放置了50年。
ja: 彼は大聖堂が所有していて50年間放置されていた古い大理石の塊を使うように頼まれました。
local: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.
native: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.

en: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.
zh: 另外兩位雕塑家曾嘗試使用它，但大理石有缺陷，被認為太窄無法雕出成功的雕像。
ja: 他の二人の彫刻家も使おうとしましたが、大理石に欠陥があり、成功する像を作るには狭すぎると考えられていました。
local: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.
native: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.

en: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.
zh: 有一位雕塑家甚至在雕像腿部之間鑿出一個大洞。
ja: ある彫刻家は、像の脚の間に大きな穴を彫ってしまいました。
local: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.
native: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.

en: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.
zh: 但別人看到缺陷，米開朗基羅看到了機會。
ja: しかし他の人が欠陥と見たところを、ミケランジェロはチャンスと見ました。
local: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.
native: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.

en: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.
zh: 由於大理石的形狀，米開朗基羅必須非常精確。
ja: 大理石の形状のために、ミケランジェロは正確でなければなりませんでした。
local: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.
native: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.

en: There was no room for manoeuvre.
zh: 沒有操作的餘地。
ja: 操作の余地はありませんでした。
local: There was no room for manoeuvre.
native: There was no room for manoeuvre.

en: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.
zh: 大衛必須側身看向一邊，因為沒有足夠的大理石讓他正面朝前。
ja: 大理石が十分でなかったため、ダビデは横を向かなければなりませんでした。
local: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.
native: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.

en: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.
zh: 大衛必須採取對立姿勢，讓他的腿能繞過大理石中已存在的大洞。
ja: ダビデはコントラポストの姿勢をとらなければならず、脚が大理石の大きな穴の周りに収まるようにしました。
local: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.
native: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.

en: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.
zh: 而且因為大理石的深度，他必須身形纖細。
ja: また、大理石の深さのために、彼は細身でなければなりませんでした。
local: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.
native: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.

en: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,
zh: 大衛與歌利亞的故事是聖經中非利士巨人被少年以色列人擊敗的故事，
ja: ダビデとゴリアテの物語は、少年イスラエル人がペリシテの巨人を倒す聖書の話です、
local: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,
native: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,

en: and only with his sling.
zh: 僅憑他的彈弓。
ja: そして彼のスリングショットだけで。
local: and only with his sling.
native: and only with his sling.

en: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.
zh: 故事的結局是大衛砍下他的頭顱，並舉起來向歡呼的人群展示。
ja: 物語の最後は、ダビデが彼の頭を切り落とし、歓声を上げる群衆にそれを掲げる場面です。
local: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.
native: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.

en: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.
zh: 傳統上，大衛被描繪成在勝利時刻，戰勝死去的歌利亞。
ja: 伝統的にダビデは、死んだゴリアテに勝利した瞬間に描かれてきました。
local: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.
native: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.

en: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.
zh: 佛羅倫斯藝術家如多納泰羅和維羅基奧描繪了他們自己的大衛版本，站在歌利亞的斷頭上。
ja: ドナテッロやヴェロッキオのようなフィレンツェの芸術家たちは、ゴリアテの切断された頭の上に立つダビデの自分たちのバージョンを描きました。
local: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.
native: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.

en: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.
zh: 所有雕像都不僅僅是表象，但米開朗基羅的詮釋將是革命性的。
ja: すべての彫像は単なる表現以上のものですが、ミケランジェロの解釈は革命的でした。
local: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.
native: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.

en: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,
zh: 通過去除聖經英雄的傳統特徵，無論字面還是比喻上都將他剝離，
ja: 聖書の英雄の従来の属性を取り除き、文字通りにも比喩的にも彼を剥ぎ取ることで、
local: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,
native: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,

en: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,
zh: 米開朗基羅也消除了將其僅僅視為故事插圖的簡單解讀，
ja: ミケランジェロはそれを単なる物語の挿絵としての単純な読み方も取り除きます、
local: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,
native: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,

en: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.
zh: 並賦予它更廣泛的隱喻意義。
ja: そしてそれにより、より広い比喩的な意味を与えています。
local: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.
native: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.

en: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.
zh: 藝術史上首次，大衛被描繪為戰鬥前而非勝利時刻。
ja: 芸術史上初めて、ダビデは勝利の瞬間ではなく戦いの前に描かれています。
local: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.
native: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.

en: This changes everything.
zh: 這改變了一切。
ja: これがすべてを変えました。
local: This changes everything.
native: This changes everything.

en: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.
zh: 首先，米開朗基羅的大衛描繪了理性。
ja: 何よりもまず、ミケランジェロのダビデは理性を描いています。
local: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.
native: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.

en: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.
zh: 大衛不是靠蠻力與歌利亞戰鬥，而是靠技巧和理智。
ja: ダビデはゴリアテと力任せに戦うのではなく、技術と理性で戦います。
local: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.
native: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.

en: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.
zh: 大衛代表了人文主義理想，即一個人僅憑智慧和意志力就能成為英雄。
ja: ダビデは、知性と意志の力だけで英雄になれる人間主義の理想を表しています。
local: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.
native: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.

en: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.
zh: 這些是文藝復興時期被視為完美的思考者美德。
ja: これらはルネサンス時代に完璧と考えられた思考する人間の美徳です。
local: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.
native: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.

en: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.
zh: 米開朗基羅捕捉到他在全神貫注思考面前挑戰的巔峰時刻。
ja: ミケランジェロは、彼が目の前の挑戦を考えている集中のピークを捉えています。
local: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.
native: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.

en: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.
zh: 大衛不再是傳統上自信的少年，而是被描繪成一個憂慮的男子。
ja: ダビデはもはや伝統的な自信に満ちた少年ではなく、不安げな男性として描かれています。
local: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.
native: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.

en: David's neck is tense.
zh: 大衛的脖子繃緊了。
ja: ダビデの首は緊張しています。
local: David's neck is tense.
native: David's neck is tense.

en: His thigh muscles are flexed, his nostrils are flared, and his brow is furrowed with fear.
zh: 他的腿部肌肉繃緊，鼻孔張開，眉頭因恐懼而皺起。
ja: 彼の太ももの筋肉は緊張し、鼻孔は広がり、眉は恐怖でひそめられています。
local: His thigh muscles are flexed, his nostrils are flared, and his brow is furrowed with fear.
native: His thigh muscles are flexed, his nostrils are flared, and his brow is furrowed with fear.

en: He is just about to glide easily and naturally into action.
zh: 他正準備輕鬆自然地投入行動。
ja: 彼はまさにスムーズかつ自然に行動に移ろうとしています。
local: He is just about to glide easily and naturally into action.
native: He is just about to glide easily and naturally into action.

en: He is tense, but contemplates the challenge ahead of him with a calculated gaze.
zh: 他緊張，但以深思熟慮的目光凝視前方的挑戰。
ja: 彼は緊張していますが、計算された視線で目の前の挑戦を考えています。
local: He is tense, but contemplates the challenge ahead of him with a calculated gaze.
native: He is tense, but contemplates the challenge ahead of him with a calculated gaze.

en: The rock is hidden inside his right palm.
zh: 石頭藏在他的右手掌中。
ja: 石は彼の右手のひらの中に隠されています。
local: The rock is hidden inside his right palm.
native: The rock is hidden inside his right palm.

en: The slingshot rests on his shoulder and hangs down his back, almost invisible,
zh: 彈弓放在他的肩膀上，垂在背後，幾乎看不見，
ja: スリングショットは彼の肩にかかり、背中に垂れ下がっていて、ほとんど見えません、
local: The slingshot rests on his shoulder and hangs down his back, almost invisible,
native: The slingshot rests on his shoulder and hangs down his back, almost invisible,

en: emphasizing that David's victory was intellectual.
zh: 強調大衛的勝利是智慧的勝利。
ja: ダビデの勝利が知的なものであることを強調しています。
local: emphasizing that David's victory was intellectual.
native: emphasizing that David's victory was intellectual.

en: His chest appears to pulse with anxiety.
zh: 他的胸膛似乎因焦慮而起伏。
ja: 彼の胸は不安で脈打っているように見えます。
local: His chest appears to pulse with anxiety.
native: His chest appears to pulse with anxiety.

en: Like all of Michelangelo's sculptures, the viewer sees David at a specific and pivotal point.
zh: 像米開朗基羅所有雕塑一樣，觀者看到的是大衛在一個特定且關鍵的時刻。
ja: ミケランジェロのすべての彫刻のように、観る者はダビデを特定の重要な瞬間で見ます。
local: Like all of Michelangelo's sculptures, the viewer sees David at a specific and pivotal point.
native: Like all of Michelangelo's sculptures, the viewer sees David at a specific and pivotal point.

en: It is not meant to be the whole story.
zh: 這並非整個故事。
ja: これは物語の全てを表しているわけではありません。
local: It is not meant to be the whole story.
native: It is not meant to be the whole story.

en: David is in motion, the position he is in is known as contrapostal or counter pose.
zh: 大衛正在動作中，他所處的姿勢稱為對立姿勢或反姿勢。
ja: ダビデは動いており、彼の姿勢はコントラポストまたはカウンターポーズとして知られています。
local: David is in motion, the position he is in is known as contrapostal or counter pose.
native: David is in motion, the position he is in is known as contrapostal or counter pose.

en: He was invented by the ancient Greeks and is a very natural and human way to stand.
zh: 這姿勢由古希臘人發明，是一種非常自然且人性化的站姿。
ja: これは古代ギリシャ人によって発明され、とても自然で人間らしい立ち方です。
local: He was invented by the ancient Greeks and is a very natural and human way to stand.
native: He was invented by the ancient Greeks and is a very natural and human way to stand.

en: The red line show where his muscles are tense and the yellow ones where his muscles are relaxed.
zh: 紅線顯示肌肉緊繃的地方，黃線顯示肌肉放鬆的地方。
ja: 赤い線は筋肉が緊張している場所を示し、黄色い線は筋肉がリラックスしている場所を示しています。
local: The red line show where his muscles are tense and the yellow ones where his muscles are relaxed.
native: The red line show where his muscles are tense and the yellow ones where his muscles are relaxed.

en: Most of the weight is on one leg, with the other leg forward, causing the figure's hips and shoulders to rest at opposing angles.
zh: 大部分重量壓在一條腿上，另一條腿向前，導致臀部和肩膀呈相反角度。
ja: 体重の大部分は片足にかかり、もう一方の足は前に出て、腰と肩が反対の角度で位置しています。
local: Most of the weight is on one leg, with the other leg forward, causing the figure's hips and shoulders to rest at opposing angles.
native: Most of the weight is on one leg, with the other leg forward, causing the figure's hips and shoulders to rest at opposing angles.

en: Giving a slight S curve to the entire torso, and therefore giving the statue a more dynamic look.
zh: 使整個軀幹呈現輕微的S形曲線，從而使雕像看起來更具動感。
ja: 胴体全体にわずかなS字カーブを与え、それによって彫像により動的な印象を与えています。
local: Giving a slight S curve to the entire torso, and therefore giving the statue a more dynamic look.
native: Giving a slight S curve to the entire torso, and therefore giving the statue a more dynamic look.

en: The story of David and Goliath would come to represent the city of Florence itself.
zh: 大衛與歌利亞的故事將代表佛羅倫斯這座城市本身。
ja: ダビデとゴリアテの物語はフィレンツェの街自体を象徴するようになりました。
local: The story of David and Goliath would come to represent the city of Florence itself.
native: The story of David and Goliath would come to represent the city of Florence itself.

en: During the Renaissance Italy was a collection of city states, each with its own ruler.
zh: 文藝復興時期，義大利是由多個城邦組成，每個城邦都有自己的統治者。
ja: ルネサンス時代のイタリアは、多くの都市国家の集合体で、それぞれに支配者がいました。
local: During the Renaissance Italy was a collection of city states, each with its own ruler.
native: During the Renaissance Italy was a collection of city states, each with its own ruler.

en: The newly independent Republic of Florence saw itself as the David of Italy,
zh: 新獨立的佛羅倫斯共和國視自己為義大利的大衛，
ja: 新たに独立したフィレンツェ共和国は、自らをイタリアのダビデと見なしていました、
local: The newly independent Republic of Florence saw itself as the David of Italy,
native: The newly independent Republic of Florence saw itself as the David of Italy,

en: holding out with unexpected strength against the meditias, and the powerful and all-consuming influence of the Pope in Rome.
zh: 以出乎意料的力量抵抗梅迪奇家族，以及羅馬教皇強大且全面的影響力。
ja: メディチ家やローマ教皇の強大で圧倒的な影響力に対して、予想外の強さで抵抗していました。
local: holding out with unexpected strength against the meditias, and the powerful and all-consuming influence of the Pope in Rome.
native: holding out with unexpected strength against the meditias, and the powerful and all-consuming influence of the Pope in Rome.

en: This point was emphasized when David was placed in a secular spot rather than its intended religious one.
zh: 當大衛被放置在世俗位置而非原本預定的宗教位置時，這一點被強調了。
ja: ダビデが宗教的な場所ではなく世俗的な場所に置かれたことで、この点が強調されました。
local: This point was emphasized when David was placed in a secular spot rather than its intended religious one.
native: This point was emphasized when David was placed in a secular spot rather than its intended religious one.

en: Commissioned as a statue of the biblical story, in Michelangelo's hands, it becomes something else entirely.
zh: 作為聖經故事的雕像被委託，但在米開朗基羅手中，它完全變成了另一種東西。
ja: 聖書の物語の像として依頼されましたが、ミケランジェロの手にかかると、それはまったく別のものになりました。
local: Commissioned as a statue of the biblical story, in Michelangelo's hands, it becomes something else entirely.
native: Commissioned as a statue of the biblical story, in Michelangelo's hands, it becomes something else entirely.

en: The proportions of David are not typical of Michelangelo's work.
zh: 大衛的比例並非米開朗基羅作品的典型。
ja: ダビデのプロポーションはミケランジェロの作品の典型的なものではありません。
local: The proportions of David are not typical of Michelangelo's work.
native: The proportions of David are not typical of Michelangelo's work.

en: The figure has an unusually large head and hands, but Michelangelo, who had dissected many cadavers, understood the human body better than any physician.
zh: 這個雕像的頭和手異常地大，但米開朗基羅解剖過許多屍體，比任何醫生都更了解人體。
ja: 像は異常に大きな頭と手を持っていますが、多くの死体を解剖したミケランジェロは、どの医師よりも人体を理解していました。
local: The figure has an unusually large head and hands, but Michelangelo, who had dissected many cadavers, understood the human body better than any physician.
native: The figure has an unusually large head and hands, but Michelangelo, who had dissected many cadavers, understood the human body better than any physician.

en: As per the commission, the statue was designed to be seen from 80 meters below.
zh: 根據委託，這座雕像是設計給80米下方觀看的。
ja: 依頼により、この像は80メートル下から見られるように設計されました。
local: As per the commission, the statue was designed to be seen from 80 meters below.
native: As per the commission, the statue was designed to be seen from 80 meters below.

en: In 2010, a fiberglass replica was temporarily placed in the spot originally planned for David,
zh: 2010年，一個玻璃纖維複製品暫時放置在原本計劃給大衛的位置，
ja: 2010年に、ガラス繊維製のレプリカがダビデの元々の設置場所に一時的に置かれました、
local: In 2010, a fiberglass replica was temporarily placed in the spot originally planned for David,
native: In 2010, a fiberglass replica was temporarily placed in the spot originally planned for David,

en: and we can clearly see that the proportions were perfectly when seen from below.
zh: 我們可以清楚地看到，從下方看比例是完美的。
ja: 下から見ると、比率が完璧であることがはっきりとわかります。
local: and we can clearly see that the proportions were perfectly when seen from below.
native: and we can clearly see that the proportions were perfectly when seen from below.

en: Nudity was unusual at the time for a biblical story, but the Renaissance was a decisive time for the nude in Western art.
zh: 裸體在當時的聖經故事中是不尋常的，但文藝復興時期是西方藝術裸體的決定性時期。
ja: 聖書の物語で裸体は当時珍しかったが、ルネサンスは西洋美術における裸体の重要な時代でした。
local: Nudity was unusual at the time for a biblical story, but the Renaissance was a decisive time for the nude in Western art.
native: Nudity was unusual at the time for a biblical story, but the Renaissance was a decisive time for the nude in Western art.

en: A renewed interest in ancient Greek and Roman art brought the human body to the forefront of artistic innovation during the Renaissance.
zh: 對古希臘和羅馬藝術的重新興趣使人體成為文藝復興時期藝術創新的焦點。
ja: 古代ギリシャとローマの芸術への新たな関心が、ルネサンス期の芸術革新の中心に人体を押し出しました。
local: A renewed interest in ancient Greek and Roman art brought the human body to the forefront of artistic innovation during the Renaissance.
native: A renewed interest in ancient Greek and Roman art brought the human body to the forefront of artistic innovation during the Renaissance.

en: A achievement in representing the body became the standard for measuring artistic genius.
zh: 對人體的表現成為衡量藝術天才的標準。
ja: 人体表現の達成が芸術的天才を測る基準となりました。
local: A achievement in representing the body became the standard for measuring artistic genius.
native: A achievement in representing the body became the standard for measuring artistic genius.

en: It is far harder to depict a nude figure than a clothed one.
zh: 描繪裸體比描繪穿衣人物困難得多。
ja: 裸体の人物を描くことは、服を着た人物よりもはるかに難しいです。
local: It is far harder to depict a nude figure than a clothed one.
native: It is far harder to depict a nude figure than a clothed one.

en: It is a myth, though, that Renaissance Europeans were comfortable with nude bodies in art, particularly when displayed in public.
zh: 然而，文藝復興時期的歐洲人對藝術中的裸體，尤其是公開展示的裸體，感到自在，這是一個迷思。
ja: しかし、ルネサンス期のヨーロッパ人が芸術の裸体、特に公共の場での裸体に慣れていたというのは誤解です。
local: It is a myth, though, that Renaissance Europeans were comfortable with nude bodies in art, particularly when displayed in public.
native: It is a myth, though, that Renaissance Europeans were comfortable with nude bodies in art, particularly when displayed in public.

en: In fact, the city fathers had a garland of 28 gilded copper leaves made to protect David's modesty, and in later years he wore a fig leaf,
zh: 事實上，市政官們製作了由28片鍍金銅葉組成的花環來保護大衛的端莊，後來他還戴上了無花果葉，
ja: 実際、市の長老たちはダビデの慎みを守るために28枚の金箔を施した銅の葉の花冠を作り、後年には無花果の葉を身に着けさせました。
local: In fact, the city fathers had a garland of 28 gilded copper leaves made to protect David's modesty, and in later years he wore a fig leaf,
native: In fact, the city fathers had a garland of 28 gilded copper leaves made to protect David's modesty, and in later years he wore a fig leaf,

en: as in this photo from the 1860s shows.
zh: 如這張1860年代的照片所示。
ja: これは1860年代の写真にも示されています。
local: as in this photo from the 1860s shows.
native: as in this photo from the 1860s shows.

en: Why is the Jewish hero David not circumcised? Again, we can trace this back to the inspiration for the Renaissance, the ancient Greeks and Romans.
zh: 為什麼猶太英雄大衛沒有割禮？我們可以追溯到文藝復興的靈感來源——古希臘和羅馬人。
ja: なぜユダヤの英雄ダビデは割礼を受けていないのか？これは再び、ルネサンスのインスピレーションである古代ギリシャとローマに由来します。
local: Why is the Jewish hero David not circumcised? Again, we can trace this back to the inspiration for the Renaissance, the ancient Greeks and Romans.
native: Why is the Jewish hero David not circumcised? Again, we can trace this back to the inspiration for the Renaissance, the ancient Greeks and Romans.

en: They regarded circumcision as barbaric, and there are no depictions of circumcision in ancient statuary.
zh: 他們認為割禮是野蠻的，古代雕像中沒有割禮的描繪。
ja: 彼らは割礼を野蛮なものと見なし、古代の彫像には割礼の描写がありません。
local: They regarded circumcision as barbaric, and there are no depictions of circumcision in ancient statuary.
native: They regarded circumcision as barbaric, and there are no depictions of circumcision in ancient statuary.

en: Also, the Catholic Church denounced circumcision in the Middle Ages.
zh: 此外，天主教會在中世紀譴責割禮。
ja: また、中世のカトリック教会は割礼を非難しました。
local: Also, the Catholic Church denounced circumcision in the Middle Ages.
native: Also, the Catholic Church denounced circumcision in the Middle Ages.

en: The Jewish figure of David has been placed into the Christian context of Florence, a hallmark of the higher Renaissance.
zh: 猶太人物大衛被置於佛羅倫斯的基督教背景中，這是高文藝復興的標誌。
ja: ユダヤのダビデ像は、フィレンツェのキリスト教の文脈に置かれており、これは高ルネサンスの象徴です。
local: The Jewish figure of David has been placed into the Christian context of Florence, a hallmark of the higher Renaissance.
native: The Jewish figure of David has been placed into the Christian context of Florence, a hallmark of the higher Renaissance.

en: It has been remarked that David's penis is rather small.
zh: 有人評論說大衛的陰莖相當小。
ja: ダビデの陰茎がかなり小さいと指摘されています。
local: It has been remarked that David's penis is rather small.
native: It has been remarked that David's penis is rather small.

en: This was considered an indication of modesty and respectability, and shows that the biblical figure is in control of his own urges.
zh: 這被認為是謙遜和體面的象徵，顯示聖經人物能控制自己的慾望。
ja: これは謙虚さと尊敬の印とされ、聖書の人物が自分の欲望を制御していることを示しています。
local: This was considered an indication of modesty and respectability, and shows that the biblical figure is in control of his own urges.
native: This was considered an indication of modesty and respectability, and shows that the biblical figure is in control of his own urges.

en: We can contrast that with contemporary images of satyrs and other figures which represented evil sexuality.
zh: 我們可以將此與當時代表邪惡性慾的薩堤爾和其他人物形象形成對比。
ja: これを、悪しき性を表すサテュロスなどの当時のイメージと対比できます。
local: We can contrast that with contemporary images of satyrs and other figures which represented evil sexuality.
native: We can contrast that with contemporary images of satyrs and other figures which represented evil sexuality.

en: David has a slight squint. It is rarely remarked on, but his eyes pointed slightly different directions.
zh: 大衛有輕微的斜視。這很少被提及，但他的眼睛略微朝向不同方向。
ja: ダビデはわずかに斜視です。あまり指摘されませんが、彼の目はわずかに異なる方向を向いています。
local: David has a slight squint. It is rarely remarked on, but his eyes pointed slightly different directions.
native: David has a slight squint. It is rarely remarked on, but his eyes pointed slightly different directions.

en: This is a typical Michelangelo trick to pull us into the eyes of David.
zh: 這是米開朗基羅典型的技巧，吸引我們注視大衛的眼睛。
ja: これはミケランジェロの典型的なトリックで、私たちをダビデの目に引き込ませます。
local: This is a typical Michelangelo trick to pull us into the eyes of David.
native: This is a typical Michelangelo trick to pull us into the eyes of David.

en: The pupils are carved out hollow to capture the changing sunlight, adding to the intensity of the gaze.
zh: 瞳孔被雕刻成空洞以捕捉變化的陽光，增強凝視的強度。
ja: 瞳孔は空洞に彫られており、変わる日光を捉え、視線の強さを増しています。
local: The pupils are carved out hollow to capture the changing sunlight, adding to the intensity of the gaze.
native: The pupils are carved out hollow to capture the changing sunlight, adding to the intensity of the gaze.

en: Michelangelo calculated every angle and always considered the position of the viewer.
zh: 米開朗基羅計算了每個角度，並始終考慮觀眾的位置。
ja: ミケランジェロはあらゆる角度を計算し、常に鑑賞者の位置を考慮しました。
local: Michelangelo calculated every angle and always considered the position of the viewer.
native: Michelangelo calculated every angle and always considered the position of the viewer.

en: The details are extraordinary. My own favourite is the jugular vein, which is swollen.
zh: 細節非凡。我最喜歡的是腦靜脈，腫脹著。
ja: 細部は驚くべきものです。私のお気に入りは腫れている頸静脈です。
local: The details are extraordinary. My own favourite is the jugular vein, which is swollen.
native: The details are extraordinary. My own favourite is the jugular vein, which is swollen.

en: This only occurs when people get excited or nervous. Michelangelo understood this over a century before scientists would describe the circulatory system.
zh: 這種情況只會在人們興奮或緊張時發生。米開朗基羅比科學家描述循環系統早了一個多世紀就理解了這一點。
ja: これは人が興奮したり緊張したりしたときにのみ起こります。ミケランジェロは科学者が循環系を説明するよりも100年以上前にこれを理解していました。
local: This only occurs when people get excited or nervous. Michelangelo understood this over a century before scientists would describe the circulatory system.
native: This only occurs when people get excited or nervous. Michelangelo understood this over a century before scientists would describe the circulatory system.

en: The veins in the raised left hand are delicate, while the veins in the hanging right hand are pulsing and more well defined.
zh: 抬起的左手上的靜脈細膩，而垂下的右手上的靜脈跳動且更明顯。
ja: 上げられた左手の静脈は繊細で、垂れた右手の静脈は脈打ち、よりはっきりしています。
local: The veins in the raised left hand are delicate, while the veins in the hanging right hand are pulsing and more well defined.
native: The veins in the raised left hand are delicate, while the veins in the hanging right hand are pulsing and more well defined.

en: The way our blood circulates, this is exactly what would happen to our own hands in the same position.
zh: 血液循環的方式，這正是我們自己的手在相同位置會發生的情況。
ja: 血液の循環の仕方は、同じ位置にある私たちの手にもまさに同じことが起こるでしょう。
local: The way our blood circulates, this is exactly what would happen to our own hands in the same position.
native: The way our blood circulates, this is exactly what would happen to our own hands in the same position.

en: Every detail points to Michelangelo's passion for human anatomy.
zh: 每個細節都顯示出米開朗基羅對人體解剖學的熱情。
ja: あらゆる細部がミケランジェロの人体解剖学への情熱を示しています。
local: Every detail points to Michelangelo's passion for human anatomy.
native: Every detail points to Michelangelo's passion for human anatomy.

en: Michelangelo, who never wasted a minute of his life, worked morning, noon and night on David, alone and in total secrecy.
zh: 米開朗基羅從不浪費一分鐘的時間，日夜獨自秘密地工作在大衛雕像上。
ja: ミケランジェロは一分も無駄にせず、昼夜を問わず一人で秘密裏にダビデ像に取り組みました。
local: Michelangelo, who never wasted a minute of his life, worked morning, noon and night on David, alone and in total secrecy.
native: Michelangelo, who never wasted a minute of his life, worked morning, noon and night on David, alone and in total secrecy.

en: At night he would attach candles to his hat. He rarely ate, and when he did sleep he slept in his clothes, which he seldom ever changed.
zh: 晚上他會在帽子上綁上蠟燭。他很少吃飯，睡覺時穿著衣服，且很少換衣服。
ja: 夜は帽子にろうそくをつけていました。めったに食事をせず、寝るときも服を着たままで、ほとんど着替えませんでした。
local: At night he would attach candles to his hat. He rarely ate, and when he did sleep he slept in his clothes, which he seldom ever changed.
native: At night he would attach candles to his hat. He rarely ate, and when he did sleep he slept in his clothes, which he seldom ever changed.

en: In 1504 he finally presented his giant to the Cathedral Committee.
zh: 1504年，他終於向大教堂委員會展示了他的巨作。
ja: 1504年、彼はついに大聖堂委員会に彼の巨像を披露しました。
local: In 1504 he finally presented his giant to the Cathedral Committee.
native: In 1504 he finally presented his giant to the Cathedral Committee.

en: They were astonished at Michelangelo's skills, and agreed it was far too perfect to be placed at such a height.
zh: 他們對米開朗基羅的技藝感到驚訝，並同意雕像太完美，不適合放在那麼高的地方。
ja: 彼らはミケランジェロの技術に驚嘆し、その高さに置くにはあまりにも完璧すぎると同意しました。
local: They were astonished at Michelangelo's skills, and agreed it was far too perfect to be placed at such a height.
native: They were astonished at Michelangelo's skills, and agreed it was far too perfect to be placed at such a height.

en: They decided to find a better location, and eventually decided it should be placed in the political heart of Florence.
zh: 他們決定尋找更好的位置，最終決定將其放置在佛羅倫斯的政治中心。
ja: 彼らはより良い場所を探すことにし、最終的にフィレンツェの政治の中心に置くことに決めました。
local: They decided to find a better location, and eventually decided it should be placed in the political heart of Florence.
native: They decided to find a better location, and eventually decided it should be placed in the political heart of Florence.

en: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.
zh: 在市政廳前的Piazza della senioria廣場，複製品至今仍在那裡。
ja: 市庁舎の前、ピアッツァ・デッラ・シニョーリアにあり、その複製は今もそこにあります。
local: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.
native: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.

en: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.
zh: 委員會的一名成員試圖說服他們將大衛放在不那麼顯眼的地方。
ja: 委員会の一人がダビデをあまり目立たない場所に置くよう説得しようとしました。
local: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.
native: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.

en: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.
zh: 他就是列奧納多·達文西。
ja: その人物はレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチです。
local: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.
native: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.

en: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.
zh: 大衛真的是一座巨像，身高近六米，重六噸。
ja: ダビデは真の巨像で、高さはほぼ6メートル、重さは6トンです。
local: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.
native: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.

en: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.
zh: 搬運雕像從米開朗基羅的工作室移動半英里，花了四天和40名工人。
ja: 彫像をミケランジェロの工房から半マイル移動するのに、4日間と40人の男性がかかりました。
local: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.
native: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.

en: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.
zh: 作為一種挑釁的姿態，大衛被放置面向南方，朝向羅馬。
ja: 挑戦のジェスチャーとして、ダビデは南向きに置かれ、ローマの方を向いています。
local: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.
native: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.

en: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.
zh: 米開朗基羅隨後在現場添加了最後的修飾。
ja: ミケランジェロはその場で仕上げの手を加えました。
local: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.
native: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.

en: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.
zh: 最初，投石器和樹樁支撐部分如這些重建圖中所示，鍍有金。
ja: 元々、スリングと切り株の支えはこれらの復元図に見られるように金で覆われていました。
local: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.
native: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.

en: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.
zh: 大衛受到佛羅倫斯人的熱烈歡迎，從一開始就被視為傑作和共和國的象徵。
ja: ダビデはフィレンツェ市民から熱狂的な歓迎を受け、最初から傑作であり共和国の象徴とされました。
local: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.
native: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.

en: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.
zh: 16世紀義大利歷史學家喬治·維薩里寫道，看過這個後，沒有人還會想看其他雕塑或其他藝術家的作品。
ja: 16世紀のイタリアの歴史家ジョルジョ・ヴェザーリは、これを見た後は誰も他の彫刻や他の芸術家の作品を見たいとは思わないと書いています。
local: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.
native: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.

en: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.
zh: 1873年，大衛被移至學院畫廊以保護其免受環境損害。
ja: 1873年、ダビデは環境被害から守るためにアカデミア美術館に移されました。
local: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.
native: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.

en: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.
zh: 1910年，一個全尺寸的複製品被放置在廣場上。
ja: そして1910年に、実物大の複製が広場に置かれました。
local: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.
native: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.

en: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.
zh: 他的無花果葉最終被移除，大衛得以以米開朗基羅原本的意圖被看到。
ja: 無花果の葉は最終的に取り除かれ、ダビデはミケランジェロの意図した通りに見ることができました。
local: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.
native: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.

en: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.
zh: 雕像的力量超越了它們最初的解讀。
ja: 彫像は最初の解釈を超えた力を持っています。
local: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.
native: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.

en: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.
zh: 一個人的英雄可能是另一個人的壓迫象徵。
ja: ある人の英雄は別の人にとっては抑圧の象徴です。
local: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.
native: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.

en: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence
zh: 米開朗基羅繼續創作許多傑作，但他奇蹟般地將一個牧羊男孩轉變為佛羅倫斯的具體化身
ja: ミケランジェロは多くの傑作を生み出しましたが、彼が牧羊少年をフィレンツェの具現化に奇跡的に変えたことは
local: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence
native: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence

en: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.
zh: 被證明是他藝術生涯中的決定性時刻。
ja: 彼の芸術的なキャリアの決定的な瞬間となりました。
local: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.
native: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.

en: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.
zh: 他是一位煉金術士，將大理石變成肉體和骨骼，並為雕塑帶來前所未有的心理洞察和物理寫實。
ja: 彼は大理石を肉体と骨に変え、これまでにない心理的洞察と物理的リアリズムを彫刻にもたらした錬金術師でした。
local: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.
native: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.

en: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.
zh: 他於1564年2月在羅馬去世，當時仍在工作，享年88歲。
ja: 彼は1564年2月にローマで亡くなり、88歳の時もまだ働いていました。
local: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.
native: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.

en: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.
zh: 他比他的藝術競爭對手列奧納多·達文西和拉斐爾都活得更久。
ja: 彼は芸術のライバルであるレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチとラファエロの両方よりも長生きしました。
local: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.
native: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.

en: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
zh: 他被帶回佛羅倫斯，葬於Santa Crocé教堂，距離他神聖的大衛雕像只有一箭之遙。
ja: 彼はフィレンツェに戻され、彼の神聖なダビデ像からすぐ近くのサンタ・クローチェ教会に埋葬されました。
local: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
native: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
